title: OpenAI o3 finds CVE-2025–37899, a remote use-after-free in the Linux kernel's ksmbd; patched in all maintained branches
summary: Sean Heelan, benchmarking o3 on ksmbd with no scaffolding, had the model surface an unknown use-after-free in the SMB logoff handler; the kernel CNA published CVE-2025–37899 on 20 May 2025.
account: The date is the CVE record's publication. Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher auditing ksmbd (the Linux kernel's in-kernel SMB3 server). He used a known bug (CVE-2025–37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 via the plain application programming interface (API), with no scaffolding, agents or tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. The Linux kernel CNA's record describes the fix (“ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”) with commits in five stable branches. Linuxiac reports the upstream response was fast and patches were merged for every maintained branch. Heelan calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model (LLM) finding a vulnerability of that nature.
purpose: General-purpose reasoning model used by the researcher to audit kernel source code for vulnerabilities.

ratings.reason: A remotely reachable kernel memory-safety bug was fixed across maintained branches before any reported exploitation. Exposure of ksmbd users is not quantified.
The kernel project received a report with a fix merged quickly, per Linuxiac.

ai_role.statement: The model produced the finding unprompted during a benchmark. Heelan selected the code, validated the report and handled disclosure. He notes the model also produced false positives in other runs. The account is the independent deployer's own, corroborated by the CVE record and third-party coverage, not by OpenAI.

evidence.title: How I used o3 to find CVE-2025-37899, a remote zeroday vulnerability in the Linux kernel’s SMB implementation
evidence.quote: I found the vulnerability with nothing more complicated than the o3 API – no scaffolding, no agentic frameworks, no tool use.

evidence.citation: CVE Program record CVE-2025-37899 (CNA: Linux), published 20 May 2025
evidence.title: CVE-2025-37899
evidence.quote: The sess->user object can currently be in use by another thread, for example if another connection has sent a session setup request to bind to the session being free'd.

evidence.title: ChatGPT’s o3 Model Found Remote Zeroday in Linux Kernel Code
evidence.quote: Upstream response was really fast, and the patches merged for every still-maintained kernel branch.

produced_by: A code slice under roughly 10k-12k lines chosen by an expert
Repeated model runs with reports triaged by a human
A maintainer workflow that accepts and patches reports quickly
must_hold: Expert curation of context and validation of candidate bugs
Tolerance for false positives across runs

headline: OpenAI o3 finds CVE-2025–37899, a use-after-free in ksmbd

comparator.against: Claude Sonnet 3.7 and Claude Sonnet 3.5 on the same 100-run benchmark (the known ksmbd Kerberos bug)
comparator.before: Claude Sonnet 3.7 finds it 3 out of 100 runs and Claude Sonnet 3.5 does not find it in 100 runs
comparator.after: o3 finds the kerberos authentication vulnerability in the benchmark in 8 of the 100 runs
comparator.quote: o3 finds the kerberos authentication vulnerability in the benchmark in 8 of the 100 runs. In another 66 of the runs o3 concludes there is no bug present in the code (false negatives), and the remaining 28 reports are false positives. For comparison, Claude Sonnet 3.7 finds it 3 out of 100 runs and Claude Sonnet 3.5 does not find it in 100 runs.

later.note: Linuxiac reported that the upstream fix was merged quickly into every maintained kernel branch, and the CVE record lists five stable-branch commits.
later.quote: Upstream response was really fast, and the patches merged for every still-maintained kernel branch.
